notes: What the turn engine needs from a game (holdem-rules provides it). A game is a pure state machine over a round: round values are opaque to the engine and JSON-serialisable. The chip ledger is passed in and returned so a game moves chips through the chip-ledger component, not its own counters. Move values are the game's own.

types.Moved: {ok:true,round,ledger}|{ok:false,code:badRequest|notAllowed|badAmount|notYourTurn|wrongPhase|notEnoughPlayers|unknownPlayer}  (a code outside the engine's error set reaches the client as notAllowed)

optionNames.returns: string[] (readable property: option names a client may switch, such as odds)

newRound.returns: {round,ledger,carry} (players are those still in, in seat order; carry is what the previous call returned, so a game can move a dealer button; the game deals, posts forced bets etc. through the ledger)

phase.returns: RoundPhase (acting: one player to move, settleMs is pacing.settleMs plus any time the game needs; auto: the table advances by itself after autoDelayMs; over: finished)

parseMove.returns: {ok:true,move,needsTurn:boolean}|{ok:false} (needsTurn false for moves allowed out of turn, such as showing cards after a round)

act.returns: Moved (auto true when the engine moves for an absent or timed-out player)

defaultMove.returns: move (what to play for a player who timed out or is away; must always be accepted by act)

step.returns: {round,ledger} (one automatic step: deal the next card, pay out, ...)

observation.returns: unknown (what that player may know; passed to the player-strategy)

publicView.returns: unknown (the game's own view for one viewer, no hidden records)

prompt.returns: {key,args,text}|null (null: the engine uses a generic prompt)
